questions.problem: What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular polygon with $16$ sides?
questions.worked_solution:
A regular polygon with $16$ sides has all its interior angles with the same measure.

The sum of the measures of its interior angles is 

$$
{180}^{∘}\times (16-2)=2\,{520}^{∘}.
$$

 

Therefore, the measure of each interior angle is 

$$
\frac{2\,{520}^{∘}}{16}={157.5}^{∘}.
$$

questions.problem: In a regular polygon, all the exterior angles have a measure of ${30}^{∘}.$ How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.worked_solution:
The sum of the exterior angles of any polygon is ${360}^{∘}.$ 

For a regular polygon, all exterior angles have the same measure. 

Therefore, the number of exterior angles is

$$
\frac{{360}^{∘}}{{30}^{∘}}=12\,.
$$

The number of sides, then, is also $12.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14193755/assets/45a75f709f4a1eb10ac610b25b38689339b00e1b8e08af54486517a1c3a9084d.png)

The diagram shows an equilateral triangle, a regular pentagon, and a regular octagon. Find the measure of the shaded angle.
questions.worked_solution:
Note, that the full angle is the sum of the measure of interior angles of an equilateral triangle, a regular octagon, a regular pentagon, and the measure of the shaded angle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14193755/assets/1289ebe280e4fc07cc71a7f45a8660c6ce29fb367567f07e1efb4d3712cbe767.png)

 

For a regular polygon with $n$ sides, the  measure of each interior angle must be

$$
\frac{{180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2)}{n}.
$$

 

 In an equilateral triangle, there are $3$ equivalent interior angles, so each has a measure of 

$$
\frac{{180}^{∘}(3-2)}{3}={60}^{∘}.
$$

Likewise, in a regular octagon, there are $8$ equivalent interior angles, so each has a measure of 

$$
\frac{{180}^{∘}(8-2)}{8}={135}^{∘}.
$$

A regular pentagon has $5$ equivalent interior angles, so each has a measure of 

$$
\frac{{180}^{∘}(5-2)}{5}={108}^{∘}.
$$

Let us call $x$ the measure of the shaded angle. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{60}^{∘}+{135}^{∘}+{108}^{∘}+x & ={360}^{∘} \\ {303}^{∘}+x & ={360}^{∘} \\ x & ={57}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

                    Finding the Interior Angles of a Regular Polygon
canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14193755/assets/830bc07f05846dcb09e360d6863387c9cc51eddc0027fe153cb2217cf7263a5a.png)

The hexagon $ABCDEF$ is regular. Find the value of $x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
A regular hexagon is a $6$-sided polygon where all the interior angles have the same measure.

The sum of the measures of its interior angles is 

$$
180^\circ \times (6 - 2) = 720^\circ.
$$

 

Therefore, the measure of  $\angle BAF$  is 

$$
m\angle BAF  = \dfrac{720^\circ}{6} = 120^\circ.
$$

The angles $\angle QAB,$ $\angle BAF,$ and $\angle FAP$ form a straight angle. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠QAB+m∠BAF+m∠FAP & ={180}^{∘} \\ x+m∠BAF+x & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2x+{120}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ x & ={30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Interior Angles of Regular Polygons
tutorials.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14193755/assets/24c4c952103f245cd4dc32e34d5dd2363478f5400ddecfbe2503130135c01946.png)

Consider the regular pentagon above. What is the measure of each interior angle?

Recall that the sum of the interior angles of a polygon with $n$ sides equals $180^\circ \cdot (n-2).$ 

All interior angles in a regular polygon are congruent. So, to calculate the measure of each interior angle, we find the sum of the interior angles and divide by the number of angles.

A pentagon has $n=5$ sides. Therefore, the sum of its interior angles is

$$
180^\circ \times (5 - 2) = 540^\circ.
$$

 

Therefore, the measure of each interior angle is

$$
\dfrac{540^\circ}{5} = 108^\circ,
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14193755/assets/a74a23a8dd760a31a0888eb694e36978c4767fd32bca6fae4fe8fe380c85e2e1.png)

tutorials.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14193755/assets/8e128a2320d2658cc61cf83a1871d09caa7e4527b684c2af9086f80a00ecc717.png)

Consider the regular hexagon above. What is the measure of each *exterior* angle?

Note the following:

- The exterior angles in a regular polygon are all congruent.

- The sum of the exterior angles of *any* convex polygon equals $360^\circ.$

So, to find the measure of the exterior angles of a regular polygon, we divide $360^\circ$ by the number of sides.

Since a regular hexagon has $n=6$ sides, the measure of each exterior angle is

$$
\dfrac{360^\circ}{6} = 60^\circ,
$$

as shown below.
